items.item: The RocksDB state backend holds in-flight data on the TaskManager's own local data directories, not only in memory.
The amount of state RocksDB can keep is limited only by the amount of disk space available.
RocksDB allows keeping very large state compared to the HashMapStateBackend that keeps state in memory.
Redis processing time is usually extremely low, in the sub-microsecond range.

at.step: Reveal: the latency budget, built at p99, hop by hop

items.item: Redis serves a single request at every given moment, so all requests are served sequentially.

at.step: Reveal: the latency budget, built at p99, hop by hop

items.item: Normal commands like GET, SET or LPUSH execute in constant, very small time.

at.step: Reveal: the pipeline strip and its correctness boundary

items.item: A budget built from average hop times looks comfortable right up until the tail arrives, which is exactly when the fallback's own cost matters.

at.step: Hook: the average looked fine, the p99 ate the budget

items.item: A budget has to be built at p99 per hop because an average hides exactly the hop that blows the deadline.

at.step: Reveal: the latency budget, built at p99, hop by hop

items.item: The chain's own measured p99 sits below the summed ceiling because the hops' latencies aren't independent of each other.

at.step: Reveal: why the chain's p99 isn't the sum of the hops' p99s

items.item: Streaming-feature state is sized by card count and window length, and past a point it stops fitting in memory alone.
A timeout fallback is a business decision with a recorded error cost, never a default to whichever branch is easiest to code.

at.step: Reveal: the fallback as a recorded business decision

items.item: Logging the exact features and decision live at scoring time lets a label arriving weeks later train on what the model actually saw.

at.step: Reveal: score-time logging and replay for retraining

items.item: At ten times the payment rate, the next bottleneck is the feature-state size and the online store's own load, not the timeout itself.

at.step: Prove it: ten times the payments

items.item: This topic leaves out model training and fraud-detection modelling, the stream engine, key-value store and model-serving internals, and the offline/online parity built in topic 23.
Latency-budget tables at p99, timeout fallbacks recorded as business decisions, and score-time feature logging are each established practice, not an emerging technique.
This topic logs what the model saw at scoring time; the next design is the feature platform that must agree with it down to the timestamp.
